# Identity test fixtures

<!-- Generated by scripts/record_identity_observations.py from tests/data/identity/observed.json (real somalier output). Do not edit by hand. -->

The identity checks (ID001 to ID005) are tested against real `.somalier` files for the Genome in a Bottle Ashkenazim trio: HG002 (son), HG003 (father) and HG004 (mother). The files are in `tests/data/identity/` (about 210 KB each) and the numbers below are what somalier 0.3.5 reported for them. They are generated, not typed.

## How the fixtures were made

- Sites: the 17,766 common hg38 sites that ship with somalier, committed here as `sites.hg38.vcf.gz` (somalier is MIT licensed).
- Autosomes: the Genome in a Bottle v4.2.1 GRCh38 benchmark genotypes for each person. A site that is absent from a benchmark VCF is hom-ref there (the VCF lists variants only), so hom-ref calls outside the benchmark's confident regions are an assumption.
- chrX and chrY: genotypes called with `bcftools mpileup | bcftools call` from the public Illumina NovaSeq 35x BAMs (GRCh38, no-alt analysis set) at the 365 chrX and 17 chrY sites. The benchmark VCFs have no chrX, and this is what makes sex checking possible.
- Each person's genotypes went through `somalier extract` as a single-sample VCF. The recipe is in `scripts/fixture_recipe/`.
- Why not extract straight from the BAMs: streaming a 46 GB BAM took hours per sample and used several GB of memory. Because the inputs are VCF-derived, the files carry genotypes only and no read depth, so somalier does not infer sex itself; ngs-preflight then falls back to the share of heterozygous chrX calls (see ID004).

## What somalier reports

Relatedness over 17,766 sites (ID002 accepts 0.35 to 0.65 for a parent and child):

| Pair | Relatedness | IBS0 | IBS2 | Sites compared |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HG002 / HG003 | 0.501 | 23 | 10593 | 17,384 |
| HG002 / HG004 | 0.495 | 32 | 10560 | 17,384 |
| HG003 / HG004 | 0.009 | 1397 | 8015 | 17,384 |

Per sample (sex is the tool's call from chrX heterozygosity; HG002 and HG003 are male, HG004 is female):

| Sample | Sex | Hom-ref | Het | Hom-alt | Unknown | chrX het | chrX hom-alt |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HG002 | male | 6,866 | 6,871 | 3,647 | 0 | 1 | 134 |
| HG003 | male | 6,895 | 6,863 | 3,626 | 0 | 0 | 129 |
| HG004 | female | 6,908 | 6,821 | 3,655 | 0 | 117 | 72 |

## Engineered failures

Each row runs the identity checks on the trio with one deliberate mistake. The findings are counts per check.

| Scenario | Mistake | Findings |
|---|---|---|
| `trio` | nothing; the true family | none |
| `duplicate` | HG002 submitted a second time as HG002_copy | ID001 x1 |
| `swapped` | HG002 (son) and HG003 (father) swapped in the pedigree | ID002 x1 |
| `wrong_sex` | HG002 declared female in the sheet | ID004 x1 |
